packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-11 - unverified image-only reading (first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of this text.
Rule note: I ran one `ls` on the three packet directories to learn the image filenames; that listing showed that packet.json exists. I did not open packet.json or anything else.

== image-001.jpg (overview, reduced) ==
Layout survey (observation): a narrow horizontal parchment strip, about 15.5 cm wide by c. 4-5 cm high against the ruler, photographed on black felt, held by a transparent pointer. A vertical fold/crease near the middle (c. 13.5 cm) divides it into two halves; small slits/sewing holes along the upper edge. Script runs horizontally, upright. Each half appears to carry at least two narrow columns of small script, so the strip looks like a horizontal slice across a two-column opening or a bifolium (tentative). Red: paragraph marks (paraphs) at several line starts, red underlining of several lines, two large red initials (a "P" left of centre, an "L"-like or "I"-like initial right of centre, and part of a red "D"/"O" at the lower right edge), and small red numerals/running numbers in the text block: ".xij." beside the P, ".xxj." (preceded by a red sign) right of centre, ".xxiij." (preceded by the same red sign) at lower right. Tentative: numbered chapters or sections with red headings. The left half is heavily abraded and faded; the right half is darker and more legible. No running titles, no interlinear gloss visible at this scale.

== image-002.jpg (tile, upper-left of strip) ==
Very faded/abraded; ink almost gone. Observed: three or four red underlines across what was the top lines of a column, small red marks (a red "I"/"t"-like stroke with dot, a red "s"-like stroke with dot), two red paraphs lower down, and the large red initial "P" followed by a red dot/flourish at the right, starting a column to the right.
image-002 l.1-4 (left column, under red rules): [illegible - ink abraded; only red underlines survive]
image-002, right column beside red P, c. 6 short line beginnings visible but cropped at the tile edge: [illegible]
image-002, lower left column, 3 lines beside the two paraphs: only isolated strokes; "... ? ... q(uo)d ? ..." not readable with any confidence -> [illegible]

== image-003.jpg (tile, centre of strip, both sides of the fold) ==
Left of fold (column beginning with the red P, which is cut at this tile's left edge; overlaps image-002 right):
image-003 L-col l.1: [red P, cropped] [illegible] ... (red) .xij.
image-003 L-col l.2: ... [illegible] ... iux(ta)? [illegible] ...ta(n)t(ur)? ... p(ro)t(?) ..
image-003 L-col l.3: ... te(m)p(or)e? cui(us)? h(oc)? ... fl(?)... fuit ...
image-003 L-col l.4: ... [illegible] ... q(ue)? fiu(n)t? ... [illegible]
image-003 L-col l.5: ... [illegible] ...
image-003 L-col l.6: ... [illegible] ... s(ed)? ... [end, short red underline]
image-003 L-col l.7: [red underlined line] ... [illegible] ... sic(ut)? ... c(om)mu(n)i?...
image-003 L-col l.8: [red underlined line, cropped by lower edge] ... [illegible]
(The ink here is abraded to a pale brown; the words above are little more than letter shapes and should not be used for matching.)

Right of fold (column with red initial; four red paraphs in the upper part, red number in line):
image-003 R-col l.1: [red paraph] [illegible, cut by upper edge]
image-003 R-col l.2: ... . fac(?) ... [red paraph] q(ui) h(ab)3(?) a(n)i(m)a(m)? ...
image-003 R-col l.3: ... [illegible] ... [red paraph] ...
image-003 R-col l.4: ... n(on) h(abe)t? ... [illegible]
image-003 R-col l.5: [illegible]
image-003 R-col l.6: [red paraph] [illegible] ... (cropped right)
image-003 R-col l.7: ... [illegible] ... (red, at line end) .[red sign resembling "ozo4" / a chapter or section siglum]. xxj.
image-003 R-col l.8: [large red initial, 2 lines high, shaped like "I" or "L" with foot] ...o(?)... p(ro)p(ter)? ... t(antu)m? q(uod) dicit? ...
image-003 R-col l.9: ... i(n) voce(m)? ... [red paraph] ... adsone(?) / a(n)i(m)e(?) ... fuit s(ecundu)m ver(um)?
image-003 R-col l.10: ... [red paraph] ad q(uo)d? sic nota(tur)? I(n) I(?) ...
image-003 R-col l.11: ... a(n)i(m)e? ... v. ca(pitulo)? dicit? cui(us)? i(n)firmit(as)? ...
image-003 R-col l.12: q(ui) b(e)n(e) p(er) ...one(m)? p(ro)? notitu(?) q(uod) e(st) si27a(?) ...
image-003 R-col l.13: ... n(on)? s(?) ... sic(ut)? ... [illegible; cut by lower edge]

== image-004.jpg (tile, right end of strip) ==
Overlaps image-003 right column at its left edge (same lines, not new text). Further right, a second column on this half, very rubbed:
image-004 far-right col l.1-7: [illegible - grey rubbed surface, only line traces]
image-004 far-right col l.8-12: four or five lines heavily underlined in red (a heading or lemma, tentative); text under the red not readable; in the last of them, red: .[same red sign]. xxiij.
image-004 far-right col l.13: [large red initial, round - "D" or "O" or "Q" - cut by the lower edge of the strip]

== image-005.jpg (overview, reduced, second face of the same strip) ==
Observation: same strip turned over; a dark glue/fold line runs along the upper edge; vertical crease near the middle. The black ink is almost entirely gone on this face. What survives is red: paraphs (one near the top left, one top right of centre, three near the lower left) and many red underlines, grouped in blocks of 3-5 consecutive lines, in at least two columns on the right half. Tentative: same text design as the other face (numbered sections with red-underlined headings or lemmata).

== image-006.jpg (tile, left end, second face) ==
image-006: no ink text recoverable. Red paraph at top (centre), red paraph + faint red traces at lower left (possibly a short red word or number, washed out), two further red paraphs at the bottom, one long red underline at right. All lines: [illegible - text effaced]

== image-007.jpg (tile, centre, second face) ==
image-007 left of fold: two short red underlines; faint grey line traces only: [illegible - effaced]
image-007 right of fold: red paraph at the top with a red underline; then four consecutive red-underlined lines, a gap of c. 3-4 lines, then three more red-underlined lines at the bottom. Ink under and between the red rules: [illegible - effaced]. A second column begins at the right edge (red underlines only).

== image-008.jpg (tile, right end, second face) ==
image-008: right-hand column: red underlines at lines c. 1-2, one in the middle, and four consecutive at the bottom; small red ticks (possibly paraph remnants). Ink text: [illegible - effaced]

== image-009.jpg (overview, reduced, a third view) ==
Observation: the ruler and a small paper label "A" are upside down in the frame, so the camera frame is rotated 180 degrees relative to the first two overviews; the writing on the strip nevertheless appears upright in this frame. It shows a strip of similar size and shape (c. 16 cm), with a wide blank area below a single band of writing along the upper edge: red paraphs, red underlines and one or two lines of ink text just under the top edge, i.e. this looks like a lower-margin strip carrying the last line(s) of two columns plus an added two-line note in the margin (tentative). Whether this is a third face (a second strip, labelled A) or the first strip re-photographed I cannot tell from the images; the outline differs from image-001 (notch at lower right), so a different strip is more likely.

== image-010.jpg (tile, upper-left/centre of the image-009 strip) ==
Main text, last lines of a column at the top edge (faint):
image-010 l.1 (cut by upper edge, red-underlined at right): [illegible]
image-010 l.2: ...? sicut? fit? p(er) modu(m)? ... [illegible] ... (then, right, red-underlined) ... [illegible] ... [red paraph] ...
image-010 l.3: ... [illegible] ... t(ame)n? i(n)? corde sup(er)? [red angular paraph/bracket] ... (then, right, red-underlined) [illegible]
Marginal note, in the blank space below the column, smaller greyer ink, two lines (an addition, hand possibly different - tentative):
image-010 note l.1: religiosis? : sin(e)? [illegible - c. 2 words]
image-010 note l.2: passi(?) ? sic(?) ... Corpus? ... [illegible]

== Limitations (packet-11) ==
- The tiles supplied render at roughly the same resolution as could be read in the overviews; letter forms are 2-4 pixels of contrast in most places. Almost nothing here reaches the standard of a checkable connected span. Every word given with "?" is a shape-guess and must not be used as evidence on its own.
- Most secure observations: red section numbers ".xij.", ".xxj.", ".xxiij." each (the last two certainly) preceded by a short red siglum that I could not resolve (four or five letters, looks like "ozo4"/"0204"; could be an abbreviated word for a division such as a chapter/distinction/question, but I cannot read it); large red initials P, I-or-L, and a round letter; frequent red paraphs; blocks of red-underlined lines.
- Tentative only: in image-003 right column, "ad q(uo)d sic", "v. ca(pitulo) dicit", "q(ui) b(e)n(e) p(er)" and a word ending "-sone(m)/-tione(m)".
- Unread: all of the second face (ink effaced); the left half of the first face; the far-right column of the first face.
- Suggested: UV or infrared/multispectral images of both faces; a true native-resolution crop (at least 3x the present scale) of the right-of-fold column in image-003 around the ".xxj." number and the large initial, and of the two-line marginal note in image-010.
- Column order across the fold is uncertain (the strip may be a bifolium slice, in which case the two halves are not consecutive text).
